newsitem.title: UK: A.Electric to bid for Yorkshire - paper.
newsitem.headline: A.Electric to bid for Yorkshire - paper.

text.p: American Electric Power, one of the United States largest electricity companies, is poised to launch a 1.4 billion pound ($2.27 billion) bid for Yorkshire Electricity at about 860p a share in cash, according to a report in the Sunday Telegraph newspaper.
An offer could come as early as this week, said the paper

"Industry analysts in New York say that AEP has spent months evaluating the British power industry and believes that this is the last chance for it to take a substantial stake in the business," said the article.
Yorkshire and Southern Electric are the only independent regional electricity companies left after a flurry of bids late last year mopped up three more regional electricity companies.
But a bid for Yorkshire has no chance of being approved before an election which the ruling Conservative government must call by May.

The Conservatives have nodded through bids for 10 regional electricity companies so far of the original 12 set up for privatisation in 1990, but the opposition Labour Party, ahead in current opinion polls, is expected to be less amenable to takeovers in the sector.
Labour has attacked so-called "fat-cat" pay awards for senior management of utilities and big dividend payouts to shareholders.

AEP is one of the 10 largest electricity companies in the United States and is capitalised at 4.8 billion stg. The group holds a 70 percent interest in a joint venture company formed to finance and build an electric generating facility in China.
Yorkshire shares closed 5p higher at 817p on Friday.
